concepts.text: Text of the Preamble
children: Opening phrase: 'We, THE PEOPLE OF INDIA'
India declared as a SOVEREIGN SOCIALIST SECULAR DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC
Justice in three forms: social, economic and political
Liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship
Equality of status and opportunity
Fraternity assuring dignity of the individual and unity and integrity of the Nation
Date of adoption: November 26, 1949

concepts.text: Four ingredients of the Preamble
children: Source of authority: the people of India
Nature of Indian State: sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic, republican polity
Objectives of the Constitution: justice, liberty, equality and fraternity
Date of adoption: November 26, 1949

concepts.text: Meaning of 'Sovereign' in the Preamble
children: India is not a dependency or dominion of any other nation
India is an independent state with no authority above it
India is free to conduct its internal and external affairs
Sovereignty includes the right to acquire foreign territory
Sovereignty includes the right to cede part of its territory to a foreign state

concepts.text: Meaning of 'Socialist' in the Preamble
children: Added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976
Indian brand is 'democratic socialism'
Mixed economy with co-existence of public and private sectors
Aims to end poverty, ignorance, disease and inequality of opportunity
Blend of Marxism and Gandhism, leaning towards Gandhian socialism
Directive Principles already contained socialist content before 1976
Congress party resolution in 1955 (Avadi session) for socialistic pattern of society

concepts.text: Meaning of 'Secular' in the Preamble
children: Added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976
Positive concept: all religions have equal status and support from state
State is neutral in matters of religion, not anti-religious
Articles 25 to 28 guarantee fundamental right to freedom of religion
Secular state contrasted with atheistic state (anti-religion) and theocratic state (state religion)

concepts.text: Meaning of 'Democratic' in the Preamble (core meaning)
children: Based on the doctrine of popular sovereignty
Supreme power is possessed by the people
India has a representative parliamentary democracy
Executive is responsible to the legislature for all policies and actions
Manifested through universal adult franchise, periodic elections, rule of law, independence of judiciary, and absence of discrimination
Embracing political, social and economic democracy in a broader sense

concepts.text: Types of Democracy
children: Direct democracy (practiced in Switzerland)
Indirect or representative democracy (parliamentary and presidential types)
India follows representative parliamentary democracy

concepts.text: Devices of Direct Democracy
children: Referendum: procedure referring legislation to the electorate for direct vote
Initiative: method for people to propose a bill to the legislature for enactment
Recall: method for voters to remove a representative before the term expires
Plebiscite: method of obtaining people's opinion on issues of public importance, often used for territorial disputes

concepts.text: Dr. Ambedkar on Social Democracy
children: Political democracy cannot last without social democracy
Social democracy is a way of life recognising liberty, equality and fraternity
Liberty, equality and fraternity form a union of trinity – liberty cannot be divorced from equality
Without equality, liberty produces supremacy of the few over the many
Without liberty, equality kills individual initiative

concepts.text: Meaning of 'Republic' in the Preamble
children: Elected head of state (President) for a fixed period of five years
Political sovereignty is vested in the people, not in a single individual
Absence of any privileged class
All public offices are open to every citizen without discrimination
Contrasted with monarchy (e.g., Britain) where head of state is hereditary

concepts.text: Meaning of 'Justice' in the Preamble
children: Three forms: social, economic and political
Justice is secured through Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles
Social justice: equal treatment without social distinctions; improvement of backward classes and women; absence of privileges
Economic justice: non-discrimination based on economic factors; elimination of glaring inequalities in wealth, income and property
Political justice: equal political rights, access to offices, and voice in government

concepts.text: Meaning of 'Liberty' in the Preamble
children: Absence of restraints on activities of individuals
Provides opportunities for development of individual personalities
Secured through Fundamental Rights which are enforceable in courts of law
Essential for successful functioning of the democratic system
Does not mean 'license' – limited by Constitution
Liberty is not absolute but qualified

concepts.text: Meaning of 'Equality' in the Preamble
children: Absence of special privileges to any section of society
Provision of adequate opportunities for all without discrimination
Three dimensions: civic, political and economic

concepts.text: Meaning of 'Fraternity' in the Preamble
children: Sense of brotherhood
Promoted through single citizenship
Fundamental Duties (Article 51-A) to promote harmony and common brotherhood
Transcending religious, linguistic, regional or sectional diversities
Assures dignity of the individual
Assures unity and integrity of the nation
Word 'integrity' added by 42nd Amendment 1976

concepts.text: Significance of the Preamble
children: N.A. Palkhivala: 'identity card of the Constitution'
K.M. Munshi: 'horoscope of our sovereign democratic republic'
Pandit Thakur Das Bhargava: 'most precious part, soul, key, jewel, yardstick'
Sir Ernest Barker: 'key-note to the Constitution'
M. Hidayatullah: 'resembles Declaration of Independence, more than a declaration, contains a solemn resolve'
Embodies the basic philosophy and fundamental values of the Constitution
Represents the grand and noble vision of the Constituent Assembly
Expresses the dreams and aspirations of the founding fathers

concepts.text: Preamble as Part of the Constitution
children: Berubari Union case (1960): Preamble is not a part of the Constitution
Kesavananda Bharati case (1973): Preamble is a part of the Constitution
LIC of India case (1995): Preamble is an integral part of the Constitution
Preamble is non-justiciable (not enforceable in court)
Preamble is neither a source of power nor a prohibition on the legislature

concepts.text: Amendability of the Preamble
children: Kesavananda Bharati case: Preamble can be amended under Article 368, but the basic features cannot be altered
42nd Constitutional Amendment Act (1976) added three words: Socialist, Secular, Integrity
The amendment to the Preamble was held valid

Pandit Nehru's 1949 statement on Commonwealth and India's sovereignty
Pledge to achieve Purna Swaraj (complete self-rule)
Commonwealth of Nations is a free association of sovereign states, terminable by free will
India's political status: dependency of British Empire until Indian Independence Act, 1947; then dominion until January 26, 1950

India declared herself a sovereign republic on January 26, 1950
